images.title: Jumps of 4 land on 8 and 20 only
images.purpose: Show that a jump of 4 from 0 lands exactly on 8 and 20 and jumps over 14 and 26, so 4 is a factor of 8 and 20 only.
images.composition: One number line from 0 to 28 with seven teal arcs for jumps of 4, and four marked places below it: two green ticks for 8 and 20 and two amber crosses for 14 and 26.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. At the top, centred at x 728 and y 70, the heading Mowgli jumps 4 at a time (48 px, bold, dark #1F2937). A horizontal number line, dark #2B2B2B, 5 px thick, at y 480 from x 100 to x 1290 with an arrowhead at the right end. 29 vertical ticks, one at every whole number from 0 to 28, 20 px tall, at x = 128 + 40 times the number, so 0 is at x 128, 8 at x 448, 14 at x 688, 20 at x 928, 26 at x 1168 and 28 at x 1248. Under every tick its number (28 px, bold, dark #1F2937), centred at y 535: all 29 numbers 0 to 28. Exactly 7 teal #0072B2 arcs above the line, 5 px thick, each 160 px wide and 90 px high, from 0 to 4, 4 to 8, 8 to 12, 12 to 16, 16 to 20, 20 to 24 and 24 to 28, with a teal dot (16 px) on the line at each landing 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28 (7 dots). A small flat boy icon (Mowgli, 90 px tall) stands above the number 0 at x 128. Below the numbers, 4 circles 56 px across at y 640: at x 448 (the number 8) and x 928 (the number 20) a green #009E73 circle with a white tick; at x 688 (the number 14) and x 1168 (the number 26) an amber #E69F00 circle with a white cross. A thin dotted grey #6B7280 line joins each circle to its number (from y 555 to y 612). Under the circles, centred at y 710 (32 px, dark): lands under 8, skips under 14, lands under 20, skips under 26. At the bottom, centred at x 728 and y 775, the text 4 is a common factor of 8 and 20 (44 px, bold, dark). No other text. Nothing else in the frame.

images.takeaway: A jump of 4 lands exactly on a number only when 4 is a factor of it: 4 is a common factor of 8 and 20.
images.description: A number line from 0 to 28 with Mowgli's jumps of 4 landing on 8 and 20 and skipping 14 and 26.
images.context: Concept image for Jumps That Land on a Number. It follows the idea of Mowgli's trail in your maths book (jumps from 0 that land on some places) and uses this concept's own example, jumps of 4 and the places 8, 14, 20 and 26.
images.teaching_notes: Say the landings out loud, 4, 8, 12, 16, and notice 14 is never said. The slip to watch is saying a jump reaches a number it has only passed over.

image_decisions.why: Seeing the landings and the skipped places on one number line is the idea that a jump size must be a factor to land on a number.
